title: bee cells drop checks claim ownership
action: Make `bee cells drop` check claim ownership the way `bee cells unclaim` does (drop-ownership D1, D2; contract drop-ownership). In packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/cells/handlers_close.rs, run_drop accepts --session-id and --force-ownership (use ownership_args, as run_unclaim does) and, inside the mutate_cell closure, calls guard_claim_ownership(root, id, trace, "dropCell", session, force) before it writes status dropped and trace.dropped_reason. Keep everything else drop does today. Declare the two new flags wherever the CLI flag schema and help for cells unclaim declares them (find it from the unclaim entry; if packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/generated/registry_payload.json is generated, regenerate it with the repo's own tool, never by hand). Write tests in the cells test module: (1) a live claim by session s1, drop called with --session-id s2 is refused with the ownership refusal and the cell stays as it was; (2) the same with --force-ownership drops the cell and appends one trace.ownership_overrides entry whose verb is dropCell; (3) drop with --session-id s1 drops it; (4) drop of a cell with no claim drops it. Watch test (1) fail on the current code before you change run_drop. No code comments.

truths: cells drop refuses a live claim held by another session and writes nothing
cells drop --force-ownership drops and records an ownership override with verb dropCell
cells drop by the claiming session, or of an unclaimed cell, drops as before
